facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

concepts.why: The patient presents with 3 months of hematochezia and two to three loose bowel movements per day with mixed blood.
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon.
A small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted on examination.
The patient has symptoms of gastrointestinal bleeding and colon polyps, which could be indicative of inflammatory bowel disease.
The patient is intermittently neutropenic, which could be a contributing factor to their gastrointestinal symptoms.
The patient is consistently lymphopenic, which could be a contributing factor to their gastrointestinal symptoms.
The patient is receiving maintenance therapy, which could be causing chemotherapy-induced colitis.
The patient's immune system is compromised due to their leukemia and chemotherapy, which could be causing immune-mediated colitis.
The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid-Schiff stains is characteristic of Malakoplakia.

rationales.F01: T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia is not directly related to the gastrointestinal symptoms.
rationales.F02: Chemotherapy can cause gastrointestinal side effects, including bleeding and diarrhea.
rationales.F03: Hematochezia is a symptom of gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F04: Loose bowel movements with mixed blood are consistent with gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F07: Neutropenia and lymphopenia are common side effects of chemotherapy.
rationales.F09: A nonbleeding external hemorrhoid could be a cause of gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F10: Negative stool studies help rule out infectious causes of gastrointestinal symptoms.
rationales.F11: Colonoscopy findings are consistent with colon polyps and gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F12: Histologic examination of the polyps revealed features consistent with malakoplakia.
